correctness.rationale: Kummer identifies V_t(n) as the number of carries adding fixed t to uniform p-adic n. Each finite carry count is a cylinder event with exact natural density. A digit d starts a carry with d/p; conditional continuation and termination give G_d(z)=(p-d)/p+d(p-1)z/(p²(1-z/p)). If fewer than g carries occur, chains cannot reach the next nonzero shift digit; disjoint digit blocks factor. At exactly g, only one chain can touch its immediately next active position, so the pairwise correction is d_i*d_(i+1)/p^(g+2) times all other zero-carry factors; this is strictly positive in the subtraction. Independently wrote a 2-state exact Fraction carry automaton, checking 192 odd-prime digit configurations for p=3,5,7, min gaps 1..4, 2-4 occupied positions and four amplitude patterns. All low coefficients and strict first corrections matched. The unbounded theorem is justified by the carry-block argument, not the finite computations.

value.rationale: This is a natural sharp interaction onset: it quantitatively explains how separated nonzero base-p digits interact in p-adic binomial valuation densities and proves the first correction cannot vanish. Extending binary shielding to every odd p and arbitrary amplitudes is structural, not a mere parameter substitution, because the exact nonzero-digit thresholds and pair weights change.

final_claim: For a fixed odd prime p and sparse shift t=sum_i d_i p^(a_i), s>=2, 1<=d_i<p, minimal consecutive occupied-position gap g, the natural density of V_t(n)=ν_p binom(n+t,t) agrees for r<g with coefficients of the product of digit-local carry G_di(z), and at r=g differs by the stated strictly negative sum of adjacent minimal-gap interaction terms.
limitations: For fixed t and odd prime p only, with at least two nonzero shift digits; formula through valuation g only.
Inaccessible older relevant source remains an originality risk, not an operational or scientific correctness failure.
